Frameworks: Popular frameworks or libraries like React, Angular, or Vue.js for dynamic, interactive user interfaces.     Integration: Using Python indirectly (e.g., through Django templates or REST APIs) to serve data to the front-end.  Back-End (Server-Side)  The back-end is where the business logic, data processing, and database management happen. With Python, this involves:      Languages: Python (as the main language).     Frameworks: Django, Flask, or FastAPI for building server-side logic and REST APIs.     Databases: Integration with relational databases like MySQL or PostgreSQL, or NoSQL databases like MongoDB.     APIs: Creating and managing RESTful APIs to handle communication between the front-end and back-end.  Full-Stack Role  A Python Fullstack Developer is skilled in:      Designing the user interface and ensuring a smooth user experience on the front-end.     Writing robust server-side logic using Python frameworks like Django or Flask.     Managing databases to store and retrieve application data.     Integrating the front-end and back-end by connecting APIs or serving data dynamically.  Why Choose Python for Fullstack Development?      Versatility: Python is easy to learn and highly versatile, supporting various domains like web development, data analysis, AI, and more.     Rich Ecosystem: A wide range of libraries and frameworks for back-end (Django, Flask) and front-end (Django Templates, Dash).     Community Support: A large community ensures readily available help and resources. Die Intelligenzprüfung unter völkischem und typologischem Gesichtspunkt Ein Beitrag zum Problem der Auslese  Von FRIEDRICH BECKER (Marburg) Mit 147 Abbildungen  Aufgabe und Ziel Die Erforschung der Intelligenz ist einer der jüngsten Zweige der Psychologie. Es sind etwa 40 Jahre her, daß dieses Problem in der psychologischen Forschung auftauchte, und seitdem bemüht man sich um brauchbare Methoden zur quantitativen und qualitativen Feststellung der Intelligenz.  Von den verschiedensten Seiten her suchte man einen Weg zur Lösung dieses Problems zu finden. Die Methoden, die man anwandte, waren außerordentlich vielgestaltig. Gemeinsam war ihnen allen nur das eine: Sie behandelten die Menschen, die geprüft und untersucht wurden, wie eine qualitativ gleichgeartete, homogene Masse.  Diese Auffassung entsprang der unorganischen und materialistischen Denkweise der „verklingenden Kulturepoche“. Es blieb unberücksichtigt, daß man keine mechanisch reagierenden Maschinen vor sich hatte, sondern lebendige Menschen, die nicht nur einen quantitativen Unterschied im Intelligenzgrad aufwiesen, sondern infolge ihrer verschiedenen Persönlichkeitsstruktur auf die einzelnen Versuchsreihen auch qualitativ verschieden reagieren mußten.  Ein zweiter Irrtum war die Überschätzung des sog. „reinen Intellekts“, d. h. einer besonderen Form des Intellekts. Dieser reine Intellekt hatte bis in die jüngste Zeit eine Herrschaftsstellung auf fast allen Betätigungsgebieten des menschlichen Geistes. Er betätigte sich einerseits im Materialismus und Positivismus und anderseits im philosophischen Idealismus, den beiden kulturellen Hauptmächten der jüngsten Vergangenheit,  Besonders verhängnisvoll aber hat sich auf dem Gebiete der Intelligenzforschung die Vorherrschaft der jüdischen Psychologie ausgewirkt. Diese nahm — zumindest ihrem äußeren Einfluß nach — hier geradezu eine Vormachtstellung ein.  Unsere Untersuchung, die das Problem der Prüfungsmethoden zum Gegenstand hat, will zunächst einmal in großen Linien zeigen, wo die Hauptschäden liegen und welche Nachteile sich für unser Volk ergeben, wenn die Ausleseverfahren nach den, bisher üblichen Prüfungsmethoden weiterhin gehandhabt werden. Vorliegende Arbeit ist eine Kritik der Intelligenzprüfungsmethoden auf der experimentellen Grundlage der Integrationstypologie von E.R. Jaensch.  Durchgeführt wurden die Untersuchungen von 1933—1936 in Marburg und Wetzlar an einem Material von insgesamt 312 Vpn., im Alter von 14 bis 35 Jahren. Sie setzten sich aus den verschiedensten Berufsständen zusammen: 151 Gewerbeschüler aus folgenden Beurfen: Mechaniker 85; Schlosser, Maurer je 5; Klempner, Austreicher, Gärtner, Schuhmacher je 4; Schmiede, Buchdrucker, Sattler, Frisöre, Bäcker je 3; Autoschlosser, Elektriker, Zimmerer, Schreiner, Schneider, Bürogehilfen je 2; Pflasterer, Metzger, Töpfer, Steinmetz, Musiker, Hausdiener j1, berufslos 7. Oberrealschüler und Realgymnasiasten aus den Klassen OIII bis OI, insbesondere aus OII und OI 65; Mechaniker (teilweise mit mehrjähriger Auslandspraxis als Feinmechaniker und Vertreter) 60; Studentinnen, Studenten und Erzieher 36.

When I do indulge it is self-destructive, and results in regret and self-loathing and shame and pain.  So... there's that, as I mentioned, that feeling of sadness for "not being able" to have that extra goodie.  There's a longing of some kind. prompt: provide all for:  Script T5MTDIH: Top 5 Movies This Day in History – December 12    1986: ¡Three Amigos!   Three out-of-work silent film actors are mistakenly recruited by a Mexican village to fend off a dangerous bandit gang.   Steve Martin, Chevy Chase, and Martin Short starred in this comedy, which cleverly mocked the tropes of old Westerns while blending physical comedy with musical elements.   John Landis directed the film, drawing from his experience with slapstick humor to create an over-the-top story with memorable scenes like the infamous singing bush.   Though not initially a blockbuster, the movie found a loyal following in later years, appreciated for its unique humor and parody style.    1997: Home Alone 3   This sequel centers on a young boy left home alone who discovers that international spies are after a secret computer chip hidden in a toy car.   Rather than reprising the original cast, the filmmakers introduced Alex D. Linz as the new lead character, updating the story with modern technology.   The traps became more elaborate, incorporating gadgets like remote-controlled planes and homemade contraptions.   Raja Gosnell, making his directorial debut, aimed to recreate the comedic tone of the earlier films for a new generation of kids.    2003: Somethings Gotta Give   In this romantic comedy, an older bachelor and a divorced playwright are thrown together after a medical emergency forces him to stay in her home.   Jack Nicholson and Diane Keaton played the leads, bringing decades of acting experience to their characters’ humorous and heartfelt exchanges.   The film explored themes of aging, love, and family with a lighthearted tone that resonated with audiences across age groups.   Nancy Meyers both wrote and directed the movie, crafting a story praised for its relatable take on finding love later in life.    2008: The Day the Earth Stood Still   An alien arrives on Earth to deliver an ultimatum about humanitys future survival in this remake of a 1951 sci-fi classic.   Keanu Reeves portrayed Klaatu, an emotionless extraterrestrial, alongside Jennifer Connelly as a scientist who tries to appeal to his humanity.   Modern special effects replaced the original’s minimalistic approach, showcasing scenes like the destruction caused by nanotechnology swarms.   The movie drew attention to environmental and ecological concerns, positioning itself as a cautionary tale for the modern era.    2003: Love Dont Cost a Thing   A high school student pays the most popular girl in school to pretend to date him, hoping it will elevate his social status.   The story examines themes of insecurity, popularity, and the pressure to fit in, adapted from the 1987 film Can’t Buy Me Love.   Nick Cannon and Christina Milian led the cast, bringing a modern, urban twist to the narrative through their performances.   The film highlighted the importance of self-worth and authenticity, finding an audience among teenagers navigating similar challenges.

I view AI not as a threat to human creativity but as a profound evolution of our tools for expression. Imagine if we had “un-invented” photography because it changed painting, or word processors because they transformed writing. In each case, the art didn’t disappear—it adapted, expanded, and reached new heights. AI offers a similar opportunity to deepen human creativity, not diminish it.

Far from making human effort pointless, collaboration with AI can help us explore uncharted creative territories, express ideas we didn’t know we could, and even reimagine what it means to be an artist. The heart of art—its emotion, meaning, and connection—remains uniquely human. With AI as a creative partner, we’re not losing our place in the creative process—we’re gaining a new perspective on what it means to create. While this shift may be difficult and even painful at times, it holds the potential to transform art and creativity into something richer, more expansive, and more inclusive than ever before. Bush’s victory.   This followed a Supreme Court decision halting the Florida recount, which had become the focal point of the dispute.   Gore’s concession speech called for healing and unity, demonstrating a commitment to the democratic process despite the deeply divisive outcome.    2003: Saddam Hussein Captured   After months of searching, U.S. forces captured Saddam Hussein near his hometown of Tikrit, Iraq. I have to figure out which of those voices aren't just imbeciles barking nonsense and which of those are genuine inevitabilities. prompt: Instructions  Tools:  To complete this assignment, you will need access to the Diet and Wellness Plus+ software app, offered with the textbook or to purchase separately. You can also share the app with others, but will need to share the password and create separate profiles for each student. The instructors will not be able to help you coordinate with other students if you choose to share the Diet and Wellness Plus+ app purchase. See the Course Resources syllabus page for more detailed information on how to purchase the software.  Recording Food Intake and Activity:  Using the Diet and Wellness Plus+ software you are to record and analyze your food intake and physical activity for three days. We have posted two demos of how to navigate the App to enter your food and activity information and generate reports.  For food intake, record all the food you eat and drink for three days, one of which must be a weekend day. Be sure to record portion sizes as well as what you ate. It is important that you enter your personal profile information BEFORE you enter foods. If you do not, you will have to re-enter the foods after you create your personal profile.  You will also record daily physical activity for the same three days. Please be sure to record the day, time, duration, and intensity of your activities using the criteria in the Diet and Wellness App. These activities should be anything you consider to be above and beyond normal daily 'routine activities'. What we mean by 'routine activities' are those basic activities that can be considered associated with BMR for the average sedentary person. So for example, we DO NOT want you to add up the times you get off the couch, the time spent watching a screen, activity associated with making your bed, making dinner, or walking to your bedroom for a nap. These activities would be captured with BMR. However, you should include all voluntary activities that normal sedentary people would not do. For example, DO include time spent studying (a lot more brain energy used than watching a show!), time spent cleaning the house, walking the dog, raking the lawn, walking to the store for a bag of chips, or playing charades. The more the better, but try to think of these activities as 'voluntary' activities that normal sedentary people would not do.  **NOTE**: If tracking your diet or physical activity is a sensitive activity for you or uncomfortable in any way, please contact the instructors to discuss alternative methods to complete the assignment.  Reports:  In order to complete the Written Evaluation, you will first need to generate two reports from the software: 3-Day  Average and Energy Balance. These reports will sum up various aspects of your diet and physical activity  relative to requirements and give you what you need to answer the questions in the written evaluation. For the  physical activity record, remember to use the same dates as the food intake record. By using the same dates,  the App will calculate energy balance automatically in the report.  Written Evaluation:  From the information contained in the 3-Day Average report (under Diet & Activity Reports), you must evaluate your diet, comparing your intake relative to recommended intakes for all nutrients. (Note that your evaluation should be based on your average intake for the three days, not based on any one day's intake). Your intake may be more than the recommended, equal to the recommended or less than the recommended. Discuss the nutrients in your assessment that you believe differ significantly from the DRI - this could be either a very high intake or a low intake relative to the DRI. It should differ enough that you believe you need to do something about it. By identifying key issues with your diet relative to the DRI, you can suggest what, specifically, you would do to correct any problems with your diet. For example, what foods need to be replaced and with what to improve different aspects of your diet. Focus on the nutrients discussed in class.  From the Energy Balance report, comment whether you are in "net positive" or "net negative" energy balance (use daily averages, not totals). Explain what would happen to your body weight if this energy surplus or deficit were to continue every day for 10 weeks.  Based on the overall results of this assignment, comment on the reliability of self-collected diet and activity data.  Please use Times New Roman (or similar) font, font size 12, 2 cm margins, and do not exceed the 2-page limit for this assignment (double-spaced).  Submission  When you submit your assignment, it must include:  1. A PDF of the 3-Day Average report. This report will include: list of foods and amounts eaten for each day; the percentage of recommended intakes for the 3-day average intake; recommended intakes for your age, sex and activity level; and report from MY PLATE which will provide you with guidance for how you might change your diet.  2. A PDF of the Energy Balance report.  3. Your Written Evaluation of your diet and physical activity, and your suggestions for improvement/changes (either PDF or DOC files are fine) (1-2 pages). I view AI not as a threat to human creativity but as a profound evolution of our tools for expression. Imagine if we had “un-invented” photography because it changed painting, or word processors because they transformed writing. In each case, the art didn’t disappear—it adapted, expanded, and reached new heights. AI offers a similar opportunity to deepen human creativity, not diminish it.

Far from making human effort pointless, collaboration with AI can help us explore uncharted creative territories, express ideas we didn’t know we could, and even reimagine what it means to be an artist. The heart of art—its emotion, meaning, and connection—remains uniquely human. With AI as a creative partner, we’re not losing our place in the creative process—we’re gaining a new perspective on what it means to create. While this shift may be difficult and even painful at times, it holds the potential to transform art and creativity into something richer, more expansive, and more inclusive than ever before. prompt: what is the tldr of this article: Toward the end of the 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump’s campaign released an unexpected ad, and one that was extremely politically effective. The tagline—“Kamala is for they/them. President Trump is for you.”—could go down in history as one of the most effective campaign slogans ever devised.  The ad reinforced a promise Trump repeated at rally after rally as he toured the swing states: If returned to office, he would immediately take on the gender ideology the Biden administration had embraced. Namely, he would end policies such as allowing males on women’s sports teams and in women’s locker rooms, and the housing of male prisoners who identify as transwomen in federal prisons for female offenders.  President Trump has addressed all this and more in an expansive executive order he will sign tomorrow afternoon called “Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government.”  Here is what the order sets out:  The Executive Order establishes Government-wide the biological reality of two sexes and clearly defines male and female.  All radical gender ideology guidance, communication, policies, and forms are removed.  Agencies will cease pretending that men can be women and women can be men when enforcing laws that protect against sex discrimination.  “Woman” means an “adult human female.”  The Executive Order directs that Government identification like passports and personnel records will reflect biological reality and not self-assessed gender identity.  The Executive Order ends the practice of housing men in women’s prisons and taxpayer funded “transition” for male prisoners.  The Executive Order ends the forced recitation of “preferred pronouns” and protects Americans’ First Amendment and statutory rights to recognize the biological and binary nature of sex.  This includes protection in the workplace and in federal funded entities like schools.  Asked why Trump is making sex-based policy a day one priority of his administration, an incoming senior administration official said, “This really was a defining issue of the campaign. The president is going to be fulfilling the promises he made on the trail.” The executive order puts it more bluntly: “Radical gender ideology has devastated biological truth and women’s safety and opportunity.”  It is becoming something of a presidential tradition to begin a term with sweeping directives regarding “gender identity.” President Biden, on his first day in office, demanded the federal government “review all existing orders, regulations, guidance documents, policies, programs, or other agency actions” that could impinge on transgender rights. Language and rules about transgender identities became embedded in the vast federal bureaucracy.  Now, Trump has ordered a reversal of all this. In an exclusive briefing with The Free Press, two senior officials provided a summary of the executive order. “Women deserve protections, they deserve dignity, they deserve fairness, they deserve safety,” said a senior policy adviser explaining why the order explicitly embraces the necessity of special treatment for women. “And so this is going to help establish that in federal policy and in federal laws.”  In reading the order, it’s clear that lawsuits challenging the new directives will start stacking up quickly. The order, for example, asserts that “All radical gender ideology guidance, communication, policies, and forms are removed.” This is far from mere symbolism. United States passports—which since 2022 have allowed citizens to choose “X” as their gender—will revert to offering exclusively male and female options, with the proviso that what people select must “reflect biological reality and not self-assessed gender identity.”  The executive order also “ends the forced recitation of ‘preferred pronouns’ and protects Americans’ First Amendment and statutory rights to recognize the biological and binary nature of sex.” When asked about how this would affect public universities, which are bound by the First Amendment’s free speech protections, the senior policy adviser said the U.S. attorney general will enforce these rights. The adviser cited a 2022 federal court ruling to the effect that a Shawnee State University philosophy professor was deprived of his First Amendment rights by being forced to address a transgender student using that student’s chosen pronouns.  The task of the Trump administration now will be to promulgate rules implementing the order, which will affect people’s daily lives. It is inevitable that activist organizations will take these matters to court. The policy adviser said the administration is ready for litigation, predicting Trump will be “100 percent successful.”  It’s a fight the new administration seems to relish. Both officials said the executive order has the potential to broaden the president’s support. “Just take a look at the polling,” the senior official said. “The public is broadly in favor of the president’s and of the Republican Party’s stance on gender. That there are two biological sexes is something that the public is supportive of.”  The executive order does not address one of the most contentious areas of transgender activism: “gender-affirming care” for minors, meaning putting gender-distressed young people on a swift course to transition and lifetime medication. The Biden administration ardently supported such treatments, even as other Western nations began to restrict them, and dozens of U.S. states began to ban them.  The Biden administration sued Tennessee over its ban. That case resulted in a contentious oral argument at the Supreme Court in December, after which most observers felt the court would probably uphold Tennessee’s law.  Asked about why the new executive order does not deal with this, the senior official said, “This executive order is the first of many. I would expect that anything the president said he would do on the trail regarding these issues, he’s going to be fulfilling those promises.”  The order ends with a sweeping statement about the fundamental issue the White House believes is at stake in this order: “Men and women are equal but have obvious sexual differences,” it reads. “If federal policies promote such an obvious falsehood that men can become women, the government will forfeit all credibility. The government must maintain a commitment to recognizing biological reality to maintain the trust of the American people.”  This order is one of nearly 200 executive actions the White House is rolling out today. Among them: orders to declare a national emergency at the border; end all DEI programs across the federal government; withdrawal from the Paris climate accord; and a return-to-office directive for federal workers. prompt: Conversation with Gemini  Closeup of Gaie Delap standing outside the Royal Courts of Justice  Prisons and probation  Just Stop Oil protester, 78, has jail term extended after no suitable tag found  Exclusive: Gaie Delap told she will have to serve 20 more days that correspond to period of time at home after recall    Diane Taylor    Follow Diane Taylor    Notifications off  Sat 25 Jan 2025 06.00 GMT  A 78-year-old climate protester has had her prison term extended for being “unlawfully at large” when government contractors were unable to find the right-sized tag for her wrist, which would have allowed her to complete her sentence in the community.    Gaie Delap, a retired teacher and Just Stop Oil protester, was sentenced to 20 months in prison for her participation in a climate protest on the M25 in 2022 and was released last November under the home detention curfew (HDC) scheme.    She was recalled to prison just before Christmas. Because of a history of deep-vein thrombosis, she could not have a tag attached to her ankle and no wrist tag that fitted her could be found.    People stand in front of Royal Courts of Justice  Keeping Gaie Delap in jail is a travesty of justice | Letters  Read more  On Friday she learned that the time she must spend in prison had been extended. Her supporters said she was shocked to receive a letter delivered to her cell saying that her time behind bars had been extended by 20 days as it corresponded to the period of time after she was notified of her recall to prison. During that time she had been at home with her suitcase packed, waiting to be arrested and reincarcerated.    Advertisement    Initially, Delap was informed she would be released on 17 March but on Friday she was told her release date had been delayed until 7 April.    The news emerged days after the Guardian revealed that the prisons minister, James Timpson, wants to reverse the rise in the number of women imprisoned, with more tagged and sent to rehabilitation centres.    Twenty-five legal, women’s and prison reform organisations and researchers have written to the justice secretary, Shabana Mahmood, calling on her to use her discretionary powers to revoke Delap’s recall, find a suitable tag for her to wear, and launch an inquiry into the systemic failures that led to this situation. Signatories to the letter include the Howard League for Penal Reform, the charity Women in Prison and the Good Law Project.    The letter questions the effectiveness of HDC, which is intended to reduce the prison population and allow individuals to reintegrate into society under supervised conditions.    “This is not a matter of public safety, as Ms Delap has demonstrated full compliance with her curfew terms. This could include completed projects, improvements to the team, or any targets you've exceeded. Understand Your Value: What sets you apart from others in your position? Are you taking on extra responsibilities, going above and beyond, or have you consistently delivered great results? Be ready to highlight these. Market Research: Research what others in similar roles with your experience and skills are being paid in your industry and location. Websites like Glassdoor or PayScale can be helpful here. 2. Know the Right Time Timing is Key: Consider when would be the best moment to bring it up. Ideally, you want to do this when the company is doing well financially or after you’ve completed a major successful project. Performance Reviews: If your company has a set schedule for performance reviews, it’s often easiest to time your request around these. If there’s no formal review process, aim for a moment when you’ve had recent successes. 3. Build Your Argument Be Specific About What You Want: Be clear about the raise you are asking for. Use your research and your achievements as the basis for your request. Rather than a vague "I deserve a raise", say something like, "Based on my recent work and the market rates for this role, I believe an increase of £X would be in line with my contributions." Demonstrate Your Impact: Show how your work has contributed to the company’s success, whether it's through improved efficiency, more revenue, or improved team dynamics. 4. Set Up the Meeting Request a Meeting: Don’t try to bring up salary negotiations casually. Set up a formal meeting with your manager or HR to discuss your compensation. Be respectful and professional when making this request. 5. Practice Your Pitch Prepare for the Conversation: Role-play the negotiation with a friend or in front of a mirror. Make sure you're confident, calm, and assertive but not arrogant. Anticipate Objections: Be prepared for your manager to push back, whether it's due to budget constraints or other factors. Have a response ready, such as offering to revisit the conversation in a few months if the timing isn't right now. 6. During the Meeting Stay Professional: Start by discussing your contributions and the value you’ve added to the team and company. Avoid comparing yourself directly to colleagues or making it about personal need. Be Open and Flexible: While it’s important to have a figure in mind, be open to negotiation. Handling the Response If They Say Yes: Great! Be sure to express gratitude and confirmation of the new terms. If They Say No or Not Yet: If you don’t get the raise you’re asking for immediately, ask for clear reasons and set a timeline for revisiting the discussion. You could also ask what goals you would need to meet to secure the raise in the future. 8. After the Meeting Follow Up: Whether the answer is yes or no, be sure to follow up with an email summarising the conversation. If it’s a "not now", thank them for their time and reiterate your commitment to contributing to the company’s success. 9. Be Ready for Any Outcome Keep in mind that negotiations don’t always go as planned. If they can't offer a raise right now, ask for constructive feedback and continue to demonstrate your value.
